name: BTC hourly-ladder fair value against trade prints (KXBTCD, crypto-fv): taker and maker, dev-only first look
mechanism: At D = close - 900 s, fair value P(yes) = 1 - G(ln(K/S0)/sigma_h) from the CF Benchmarks index average S0 and a volatility scaled to 880 s (M1 Deribit DVOL x 0.872, M2 realised vol x 1.033, M3 mean of the two with a two-normal mixture). Taker: the first same-side taker print in (D+5 s, D+180 s] if 100 x (fair - price) - fee >= margin (3c or 6c) and price in [0.03, 0.97]; a 10-lot order 5 s later fills at the next same-side print within 120 s with size >= 10; hold to settlement; at most 3 orders per event. mechanism: Pump.fun creator fee sharing (2026-01) lets a creator split fees across up to 10 wallets and revoke update authority; since 2026-03 one post-launch redirect is allowed and then the settings lock. A creator who splits fees to many wallets and locks, or revokes authority, is paid from volume, not from a dump, so the dump-and-leave incentive is weaker; a creator who never configures it or redirects once to a single fresh wallet is the opposite. This is a veto/label feature for books we already screen (owner priority: real rug / big-loser filter with new information), not a signal to buy.

Original kill-risk note: Capacity guess: a veto on an existing book's entries: if it removes 10% of entries that carry 25% of losses, on a 20 trades/day x 0.1 SOL book that is up to 0.05 SOL/day of avoided loss (arithmetic on invented shares, not a measurement). Kill risk: most pump coins never configure sharing, so the label is almost constant; creators can set it to wallets they own (sybil); the Haiku v3 veto test showed learning near placebo, so the gain may be only the dead-pool filter already captured. Neighbours: lib-c-R2.SB-H10, web-pump-changes-3, lp-fees-1, hunt23-w3-qsink-1. P62 facts. The label is the fee-program SharingConfig PDA (seeds sharing-config + mint, program pfeeUx...); it is not in our tape. Today's state of 200 sampled coins: PDA exists 16 (8%), absent 184 (92%); 15 of the 16 have one shareholder, 16 of 16 admin_revoked. That is today's state, not causal. Step 2 (job #1707 at b6bec68e, N=300 per split vs 'up to 400' in the prereg; 286 discovery / 299 confirmation usable): the registered detector (CreateFeeSharingConfig in the create tx logs) found cfg=1 in 0 of 585; veto_share 1.0, AUC 0.5, placebo 0.5; bl_rate 0.7307692307692307 / 0.5919732441471572 (label too loose, 59-73%); bl_rate_cfg1 null (n_cfg1 = 0). Positive control (a), p62_poscontrol_b.py: for the 16 step-1 configured coins the config transaction was found for 13 (oldest 5 PDA signatures, log 'Instruction: CreateFeeSharingConfig'); the committed detector returned 1 on all 13, and none of the 13 config signatures equals the coin's create signature (FcDNQrtL: create 2V9TF3h8..., config 48mKQ1BA..., 0 s later). Delays 0 s (2: FcDNQrtL, 2kQ1iKd9), 1-2 s (9), 31 s (1), 69 s (1). So the detector works, and the config is a separate transaction from the create transaction: a real configured coin is invisible to an in-create-tx test. The KILL stands for the in-create-tx feature: the registered detector found none in the pre-registered sample, and 0 of 13 configured coins had the config in the create transaction. 3 coins had no config tx found (uJyBTLgd, 6CNTn9gT, AnHSooEv; RPC/window limits).
